questions.stem: OHM'S LAW states the relationship V = IR. The unit of resistance R is the:

options.option_text: Ampere, the unit of electric current flowing
Ohm, equal to one volt per ampere ratio
Volt, the unit of potential difference
Watt, the unit of power dissipated as heat

questions.explanation: OHM (Ω) — unit of resistance. 1 Ω = 1 V/A. Volt = unit of voltage / EMF. Ampere = unit of current. Watt = unit of power (P = VI). Ohm's law applies for OHMIC conductors (linear V-I); not for diodes / non-linear materials.

questions.stem: Three resistors of 6 Ω, 6 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in PARALLEL. The equivalent resistance is:

options.option_text: 18 Ω, the sum of all three resistor values
2 Ω, equal to one resistor divided by three
6 Ω, the same as a single resistor's value
9 Ω, average of three resistors plus one

questions.explanation: Parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ = 3/6 = 1/2 → R = 2 Ω. For n equal resistors of value R in parallel: R_eq = R/n. Distractor 18 = SERIES sum (R₁+R₂+R₃). Distractor 6 ignores parallel combination. Distractor 9 from arbitrary mistake.

questions.stem: The MAIN difference between DC (Direct Current) and AC (Alternating Current) is that DC:

options.option_text: Flows in one constant direction throughout time
Periodically reverses direction at fixed frequency
Cannot transmit any power at long distance ever
Is generated only by lightning during thunderstorms

questions.explanation: DC — current flows in ONE direction (e.g., from a battery, solar cell). AC — current periodically reverses direction (sinusoidal in most distribution; 50 Hz in India, 60 Hz in US). DC: simpler for electronics, batteries, electroplating. AC: easy to step up/down with transformers → ideal for long-distance transmission. HVDC links exist for very long distances. Distractor 2 describes AC, not DC. Distractors 3, 4 are false generalisations.

questions.stem: The frequency of household AC supply in India is:

options.option_text: 60 Hz, the standard used in North America
50 Hz, the standard used across most of India
100 Hz, twice the European standard rate
25 Hz, used in heavy electric traction systems

questions.explanation: India: 50 Hz, 230 V (single phase) / 400 V (three phase). Most of the world (Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia): 50 Hz. North America (US, Canada, parts of Latin America), Japan east of Mt Fuji: 60 Hz. Choice was historical — Westinghouse + Tesla picked 60 Hz, the rest of the world standardised at 50 Hz. Distractor 4 — 25 Hz was used in older Indian railway traction (now mostly converted).

questions.stem: An electric heater of 1000 W is used for 5 hours. Energy consumed in kilowatt-hours (kWh) is:

options.option_text: 1 kWh, equal to a thousand watt-seconds total
5 kWh, equal to five units of electricity used
10 kWh, double the actual energy used
50 kWh, equivalent to a month's heavy use

questions.explanation: Energy = Power × Time = 1 kW × 5 h = 5 kWh. Each kWh = 1 'unit' of electricity in commercial billing. Cost ≈ ₹5-10/unit in India depending on tariff slab. Distractor 1 from forgetting to multiply by hours. Distractor 3 doubles. Distractor 4 way off.

questions.stem: A FUSE in an electrical circuit is designed to:

options.option_text: Step up the voltage from low to high values
Melt and break the circuit when current is excessive
Convert AC to DC for use in electronic appliances
Store electrical energy for later use as needed

questions.explanation: FUSE — a thin wire of low-melting alloy (tin-lead, zinc) chosen so it melts when current exceeds a rated value (commonly 5 A, 10 A, 16 A). Breaks the circuit, protecting wiring + appliances from overheating + fire. Once blown, must be replaced. Modern equivalents — MCB (Miniature Circuit Breaker) which trips and can be reset; ELCB / RCCB — earth-leakage protection. Distractor 1 = transformer. Distractor 3 = rectifier. Distractor 4 = capacitor / battery.

questions.stem: The RMS (root mean square) value of an AC voltage with peak value 311 V is approximately:

options.option_text: 440 V, the peak times root two
220 V, the peak divided by root two
311 V, the peak value itself
156 V, half of the peak value

questions.explanation: For sinusoidal AC: V_rms = V_peak / √2 ≈ V_peak × 0.707. So 311 / √2 ≈ 220 V — matches the household supply rating in India. RMS represents the equivalent DC voltage that would dissipate the same power in a resistor. Distractor 1 multiplies by √2 (gives peak from RMS). Distractor 3 = peak itself. Distractor 4 = peak/2 (incorrect formula).
